packets.title: model-gateway: a Do run's stream registers with the cancel registry and the run-control bus, so Stop (local, durable or from a peer replica) stops the run
tests: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/dev/mp-target-w2 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -q -p model-gateway --lib agentic
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/dev/mp-target-w2 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -q -p model-gateway --lib run_control
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/dev/mp-target-w2 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -q -p model-gateway --lib cancel
packets.brief:
Register row D1-229 (P1, blocks Wave 1): `agentic_run_stream` (apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/sse.rs, `fn agentic_run_stream(` ~:10828) registers nothing with the cancel registry or the run-control bus. The Ask path does both before `connected` (sse.rs ~:2586-2599: `cancels.register_run(&request_id, &org_id, &user_id, &session_run.run_id)` then `state.run_control.attach(&cancels, &state.queued_inputs, &request_id, &session_run.run_id).await`) and observes the flag in its loop (~:3719, emits `ChatEvent::Stopped { reason: "client cancelled" }`).

What that means today, read from the code by the lead: (a) POST /v1/invoke/{request_id}/cancel on a Do run finds nothing; (b) the durable route POST /v1/orchestration/runs/{run_id}/cancel (http_routes.rs `async fn cancel_run` ~:1962) marks the run cancelled in Session Core, but `state.run_control.cancel_run(...)` returns NoOwner for it, locally and from a peer replica; (c) the Execution Core RunAgent call keeps running in the dispatch task that `follow_agentic_run` (~:10727) follows, until the loop ends by itself. Execution Core's own latch (execution-core/src/grpc.rs `cancel_run` ~:1657) is never read by the loop; its `run_agent` handler (~:1726) runs the loop inside the request future, so dropping the client call is what stops it (execution-core agent.rs test ~:27849: dropping the request's future is what a cancelled request does). So Stop does not stop a Do run, and `/continue` segments (which also go through `agentic_run_stream`) are not reachable over the run-keyed subject.

Do, in sse.rs (CRLF or LF: measure the file and keep it):
(1) Inside the spawned task of `agentic_run_stream`, before the `connected` frame is sent: register with `state.cancels.register_run(&request_id, &org_id, &user_id, &run_id)` and call `state.run_control.attach(&state.cancels, &state.queued_inputs, &request_id, &run_id).await`, the same calls the Ask path makes. Do NOT register the stream in `queued_inputs`: no agent loop drains mid-run input, and a registration would accept a message nobody reads (see `finish_stream_registrations`' doc ~:59-85). Read run_control.rs `attach` to see what it does for a request that has no queued-input registration: a peer-delivered input for it must be refused or dropped visibly, never acknowledged as delivered; if attach would acknowledge it, fix that narrowly and say so in your report.
(2) Release the registration with a drop guard owned by the task (cancels.finish(&request_id), plus any detach run_control needs: check whether attach leaves something that finish does not remove). Not a manual call at each exit: the task has about ten exits, and the last bug of this kind (D1-795, a gauge counted by hand) leaked on every stopped stream.
(3) Give `follow_agentic_run` a cancel input (for example the `Arc<AtomicBool>` from register_run, checked on a short tokio interval of about 100-200 ms inside the same `select!`, or a future that resolves when it flips) and a distinct cancelled outcome. On cancel: `dispatch.abort()` so the gRPC call to Execution Core is dropped, and return. Order in the biased select: the dispatch result first (a run that finished in the same poll wins over a cancel), then cancel, then the deadline. The deadline keeps its current meaning exactly (it detaches the dispatch, never aborts it); keep its tests unchanged.
(4) In `agentic_run_stream`, on that cancelled outcome: send the same terminal `stopped` frame the Ask path sends (`ChatEvent::Stopped { reason: "client cancelled".to_owned() }`, sent the way this function sends its other ChatEvents), and leave the run cancelled in Session Core: call Session Core's RunService CancelRun for `run.run_id` with the model bearer and reason "user_requested", built like http_routes.rs `cancel_run` builds it (~:1990-2000, `authenticated_session_request` with `CancelRunRequest`). It is idempotent: after a durable cancel it answers already-terminal, which is fine. A failure is a warn log with the run id and code only, never a second terminal frame. Close the attempt on the run subject the way the other exits of this function do after RUN_STARTED (~:11086); use an existing cancelled event type if the code has one, do not invent a new type (say what you used). A park continue (`parking`) that is stopped is cancelled the same way (a Stop is the user's explicit choice); say so in a comment.
(5) Do not change the Ask path, the deadline behaviour, the two tool loops, or Execution Core. ZDR: logs carry ids and codes only.

Tests (unit tests next to the code, in the file's existing test modules):
- follow_agentic_run: the flag flips while the dispatch is pending -> cancelled outcome, and the dispatch task is aborted (prove it, e.g. a future holding a guard whose Drop sets a flag, or JoinHandle::is_finished after a yield); dispatch ready and flag set in the same poll -> the result wins; the existing deadline tests unchanged and green.
- run_control: a peer cancel by run id (the pattern of the tests near run_control.rs ~:1500-1660 that use `owner_cancels`) reaches a stream registered exactly the way agentic_run_stream now registers it (register_run + attach, no queued-input registration): this is the cross-replica Stop of a Do run.
- a source-shape test in sse.rs's tests (pattern: `code_of("fn agentic_run_stream(", "\n}\n")` ~:20532 and `item_text` ~:19250): register_run and run_control.attach appear before the `connected` send, a guard releases them, and no bare `cancels.finish(` sits at the exits.
Run the tests listed in the task record; report what you ran and the counts. Keep the final report short and call the structured output before you stop.

packets.title: ZDR goldens: MCP is never offered, executed or observed for any ZDR row of the posture matrix, driven by the vendored matrix through each plane's real gate
tests: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/dev/mp-target-w2 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -q -p execution-core --test zdr_mcp_golden
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/dev/mp-target-w2 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -q -p model-gateway --test zdr_mcp_observation_golden
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/dev/mp-target-w2 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -q -p model-gateway --test zdr_posture_matrix
bash scripts/tests/zdr-contract-sync.test.sh   (from the repository root; read-only, must stay green)
packets.brief:
Register row D1-007 (P1, blocks Wave 1) asks for the ZDR goldens `mcp_tool_observation_under_zdr` and `mcp_tools_under_zdr_not_offered_not_executed` (build plan docs/plans/model-plane-chat-build-plan-2026-10-14.md, WS05 'ZDR clause and regression guards', ~:537: under ZDR MCP is never offered and never executed, typed refusal key `mcp_execution`; the observation write is skipped for a ZDR caller).

Lead's design decision (do not deviate): the goldens are NOT new rows of apps/Model Plane/api/contracts/zdr-posture-matrix.json. That file has a closed three-table schema read by seven loaders in four planes (auth-core, the BFF, conversation-core, integration-corev2 among them; see scripts/tests/zdr-contract-sync.test.sh CONSUMERS ~:298-305), each of which rejects unknown fields, and MCP is a consequence of the enforcement decision, not a new posture input. So each golden is a test in the plane that owns the MCP gate, which iterates EVERY `enforcement_rows` row of that plane's vendored matrix copy (rust/services/execution-core/tests/fixtures/zdr-posture-matrix.json, rust/services/model-gateway/tests/fixtures/zdr-posture-matrix.json), drives the row's bearers and route through the plane's real decision (model-gateway's tests/zdr_posture_matrix.rs already loads the matrix and runs `zdr_posture::decide` then normalize: reuse that loading code or pattern; execution-core has a durable-loop ZDR matrix test that loads its copy, find it) and then through the plane's REAL MCP gate, never a reimplementation. Do not edit any zdr-posture-matrix.json or .sha256 file (so nothing needs re-vendoring).

1. `mcp_tools_under_zdr_not_offered_not_executed` in a new execution-core integration test file (or the existing test file that already loads the matrix, if adding there is cleaner; then adjust the task's new_files in your report). The gates: execution-core runtime_loop/mod.rs `feature_not_supported("mcp_execution")` at ~:716, ~:1426, ~:3256, ~:3947, and wherever MCP (`mcp__*`) tools are merged into the tool set a run offers the model. For every enforcement row whose resolved decision is zdr: no `mcp__*` tool is offered, and an MCP call is refused with the typed `mcp_execution` refusal. For the waived decision: assert what the code does today and cite the line in a comment; never invent a rule. For persistent rows: MCP is offered when configured, so the test cannot pass vacuously. Assert the number of zdr rows driven is > 0 and print the counts. If the gate is only reachable through private items, use the narrowest existing pub(crate)/test seam or a small `#[doc(hidden)] pub` helper the crate already uses for tests; say what you exposed.
2. `mcp_tool_observation_under_zdr` in a new model-gateway integration test: the gate is the observation write in model-gateway src/capability_observation.rs (its unit test `mcp_tool_observation_under_zdr_never_happens` ~:495 covers one hand-built case) and the gRPC check src/grpc.rs ~:1963 `require_explicit_zdr_contract(&identity, "mcp_execution")`. Drive every enforcement row: a zdr decision writes no observation (and the gRPC MCP path is refused, typed); a persistent decision writes one. Same non-vacuity rule.
3. Add a short paragraph to apps/Model Plane/api/contracts/README.md under `## zdr-posture-matrix.json`: the two MCP goldens, where they live, that they drive the enforcement rows of the vendored copy, and why they are not rows of the matrix (the closed cross-plane schema).
4. From the repository root run `bash scripts/tests/zdr-contract-sync.test.sh`; it must stay green.

Another packet edits model-gateway/src/sse.rs, run_control.rs and cancel_registry.rs in the same tree at the same time: never touch those files. If model-gateway fails to compile because of an error in one of them, wait a few minutes and retry, and mention it in your report. Keep the final report short and call the structured output before you stop.
